entry.title: v0.13.4
entry.content:
Added

  • Bring your own computer with Tether. Tether turns your own computer into part of Open WebUI: models from Ollama, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible server, OpenAPI and MCP tool servers and Open Terminal servers that you add in the Tether app now show up just for you in the model selector, the Tools list of the + menu and the terminal menu of any Open WebUI you connect, from whatever device you open it on, and Open WebUI reaches them through Tether, so their addresses, commands and keys never leave your computer. This needs Tether 0.1.14 or later, or 0.1.16 for MCP servers, tool servers and terminals need "ENABLE_TOOL_SERVERS" turned on, and a Tether model whose ID matches a model already in Open WebUI stays hidden. Tether replaces Direct Connections. #34397
  • Sandboxed agents on your own computer. Tether 0.1.13 or later can lock the terminal on your computer into a sandbox, so models and coding agents work in your real files without reaching the rest of your machine: on macOS and supported Windows devices, Open Terminal and everything it launches, coding agents included, can only touch the one folder you pick, run offline unless you turn on Network access and accept no incoming connections, with no Docker, virtual machine or administrator setup needed. If the sandbox cannot be enforced, the terminal stays stopped instead of quietly running without it, and browser and desktop control stay off while it is on. Turn it on in Tether under Settings > Open Terminal > Sandbox.
  • Local MCP servers through Tether. Open WebUI can now use MCP servers that run as a local command over stdio, the way many MCP servers are distributed, by launching them on your computer through Tether 0.1.16 or later, with no proxy such as mcpo and no port to open. Add one in Tether under Settings > Integrations > Tools with its command, or connect an MCP server by its web address, and pick it from the Tools list of the + menu. Local commands run with your own account's access, outside Tether's workspace sandbox.
  • A computer for every user. With Terminals 0.4.0 or later connected, Open WebUI now hands out sandboxed computers on demand: anyone with Write access to the connection can create a terminal right from the terminal menu of the message input, pick whether everyone shares one machine or each user, chat or model gets its own, and set its image, CPU, memory, storage, network profile, environment variables, start directory and a setup script that, for example, clones a repository and installs its dependencies, without an administrator setting up each one. Terminals can be shared with users and groups and their instances started, stopped, restarted or deleted, a View files option opens any terminal's files without selecting it for the chat, System info shows how the setup script went, and those who manage a terminal can open the files and system info of other people's running instances. Start and Stop need Terminals 0.4.1 or later, the start directory and setup script need Open Terminal 0.17.7 or later in the terminal's image, and network profiles are the ones an administrator defined with "TERMINALS_NETWORK_PROFILES".
  • Coding agents as chat models. Coding agents now work much like any other model in the chat. Hermes, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Goose and Qwen Code join Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Cline, Gemini CLI and Pi, and any other ACP agent added to Open Terminal with "OPEN_TERMINAL_ACP_AGENTS" works as well, once it is installed and signed in on the terminal. Auto for tool permissions now lets Codex, Claude Code and Grok approve routine actions themselves and pass on only what they escalate, and the reasoning effort in the advanced parameters now also applies to Claude Code, Pi and ACP agents that offer effort levels, such as OpenCode, which stop with an error when the chosen level is not offered for the model. Replies can now be regenerated and earlier messages edited, and a forked or cloned agent chat picks up where the original left off: Codex continues its own conversation from that point, other agents start over from the chat so far, and file changes the agent already made stay. Claude Code continues its own conversation too with the next Open Terminal release after 0.17.20 and until then asks you to update Open Terminal instead. The new agents and Auto for Claude Code and Grok need Open Terminal 0.17.19 or later, and effort for Claude Code, Pi and ACP agents needs 0.17.9 or later. #34167
  • Pages open as tabs. Notes, channels, the workspace, automations, the calendar, the playground, the home page and new chats from pinned models now open as tabs beside the current chat when you click or drag them from the sidebar, pick them in the user menu or follow a link to one of them in a chat message, and starting a new chat, also from a sidebar folder, keeps the open tabs.
  • Queued messages steer replies. A message you send to your own chat while a reply is still running now waits on the server, so it is kept when you leave the page, and the reply wraps up at its next step so your message is answered right away with what it has done so far.
  • Instant first message. The first message of a new chat now shows up right away while the chat is still being created, instead of only once it exists, unless files are still being uploaded with it.
  • Full chat in side chats. Side chats now run the same chat as the main view, so message buttons, sources, token usage, follow-up suggestions, slash commands, queued messages, chat variables, web search settings, tool events such as code execution and input requests, HTML and SVG previews, notifications while the window is in the background, unsent text after a page reload and answers from several models at once now work there too, and a side chat's tab now has the chat menu. #34064, #34165, #34147, #34031
  • Interactive visualizations. Models can now draw interactive charts, diagrams, calculators and explainers right in the chat with the new Visualizations built-in tool, which is off by default and turned on per model under Builtin Tools, and administrators can rewrite its instructions under Admin Settings > Interface > Visualization Prompt or with "VISUALIZATION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE".
  • Video generation. Models can now generate videos with a built-in tool, also starting from an image in the chat, once an administrator turns on Video Generation under Admin Settings > Videos, adds connections to OpenAI, LiteLLM or OpenRouter, which offers models such as Veo and Kling, with a default video model, per-model defaults and access settings, and grants the Video Generation permission, which is off by default, after which users turn on Video in the + menu, can pick the model there and watch the result in the chat. #13780, #13927
  • Several image models. Administrators can now add several image connections under Admin Settings > Images, each an OpenAI-compatible server such as LiteLLM, Gemini, ComfyUI or AUTOMATIC1111 with its own models, sizes, workflows and access, used for generating images, editing them or both, where OpenAI-compatible ones offer the same sign-in options and custom headers as model connections and list the image models of a LiteLLM server by themselves when no model IDs are entered, choose the default generation and edit models and give a model its own default image model in its settings, and users with more than one image model pick one from the Image entry in the + menu of the message input. #10344
  • Git panel becomes a GitHub workbench. With Open Terminal 0.17.8 or later and the GitHub CLI signed in on the terminal, as included in the full, agents and cuda images, the Git panel now covers the whole GitHub loop: browse, search, create, edit, comment on, close and reopen the repository's issues, see each pull request's checks, review state, labels, activity and conflicts with a status filter and a choice of merge method, and search issues and pull requests across the whole repository instead of only the loaded list. Buttons such as Work on this, Fix, Address feedback and Resolve conflicts in chat hand the issue, review or conflict to the model as a ready-made request in the message input, and changed files can be picked with Ctrl or Shift click to discard several at once or all of them.
  • Terminals follow your chats. Each chat now saves its terminal and working folder and switches back to them when you reopen it, including a terminal you turned off, and administrators can pick a default terminal under Admin Settings > Models > Model Defaults that new chats start with for every model without a terminal of its own, so every chat can start with a computer attached. Chats from earlier versions open without a terminal unless they are coding agent chats.
  • Folder chat board. Folder pages now list their chats with a search through titles and messages and filters for status, tags, people, activity and last update, and can show them as a board with columns and rows by status, tag or activity such as unread, generating or waiting for approval, gives each chat there the sidebar's chat menu to rename, move, archive or delete it, and a folder's badge in the sidebar now also counts chats waiting for approval. #33771
  • Chat statuses in folders. Folders can now set up statuses for their chats under Edit statuses, with Backlog, To do, In progress, Waiting and Done offered as suggestions, chats then get a status from their menu on the folder page or by dragging them between board columns, people who can edit a shared folder can set the status of every chat in it, and each chat shows how long it has been in its status.
  • Folder automations. Folder pages now have an Automations section that lists the folder's automations with their state and last run and creates new ones there, chats made by an automation are marked with a clock, and automations can now post into shared folders their creator can edit, where everyone who can edit the folder can pause and run them and see their runs.
  • Knowledge on folder pages. Folder pages now have a Knowledge section that lists the knowledge bases, notes, chats and files new chats in the folder can use, where you can add, upload, drop, open and remove them.
  • Colored chat tags. Tags can now get a color on the folder page that applies wherever the tag is used, and the chat menu has a Tags submenu to find, add and create tags, and people who can edit a shared folder can tag every chat in it.
  • Edit automations in place. An automation's page now edits its name, instructions, status, schedule, model, terminal and destination right there with a Save button that appears once something changed, shows saved instructions collapsed behind Show more, lists its runs as activity below, and has Copy link and Duplicate in its More menu.
  • Readable agent and terminal steps. Steps of coding agents and the terminal tool calls of other models now show in the chat as what they did, a command with its output and its exit code when it failed, a diff of each edited file with its added and removed lines, or the files read, code and web searches, folders listed and pages fetched, and a group of steps is summarized as for example Ran 2 commands, Edited 1 file, Read 3 files. Diffs of files that other models edit through the terminal tools need Open Terminal 0.17.20 or later.
  • Models can mention people. With the Chat History built-in tool, models can now look up users by name or email and mention them in a reply, and each mentioned user who can see the chat gets an inbox notification that opens the chat at that reply.
  • OpenAI-compatible vector stores. External knowledge sources under Admin Settings > Integrations can now be OpenAI-compatible vector stores on OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or LiteLLM, searched on the server so no matching embedding model is needed, and you either pick one or more stores for a knowledge base or turn on 'List stores as knowledge bases' to show every store of the connection, or only chosen ones, as read-only knowledge bases that stay in sync with the endpoint and share the connection's access settings.
  • Review settings before saving. Admin settings pages now show next to Save how many settings changed since they were loaded or saved, and clicking that count or Save lists every change with its old and new value to confirm, with passwords and API keys kept hidden. #34534, #34532
  • Smoother replies with code blocks. Long replies with many code blocks no longer stall the tab a little longer with every new code block while they stream, so a reply with 300 code blocks that arrives at once now shows in 9 seconds instead of more than two minutes. #34495, #34492
  • Faster large PDF previews. Long PDFs in the file preview now open in about a second and use far less memory, because only the pages near the screen are drawn and pages far away are released, so a 1500-page manual no longer takes over half a minute and a large scanned file no longer pushes the browser past many gigabytes. The browser's find (Ctrl+F) now only matches text on pages near the screen. #34602, #29576
  • Faster folder reopening. Reopening a folder now shows its chats, details and coding agent models right away from what was already loaded and refreshes them in the background, sidebar folders keep their loaded chats when collapsed and expanded again, and folder chat lists update immediately when a chat is renamed, moved, archived or deleted.
  • Faster model list with Redis. With Redis, the model list now loads faster and Redis no longer keeps a copy of every model profile image, which helps most with large animated or imported images, and Functions and Tools now receive the model without its profile image. #34595, #34594
  • Faster profile pictures and knowledge exports. Large profile pictures of users, models and channel webhooks and knowledge base exports are now sent in one piece, so a 2 MB picture loads in about 15 ms instead of a few hundred and a page full of large avatars no longer takes seconds, and exporting a knowledge base no longer holds up other users' requests on the same server process while the archive is packed. #34598, #34597, #34600, #34599
  • Shared chat terminals. People who can reply to a chat shared with Allow replies can now work in that chat's terminal, as the share dialog now points out: with a Terminals template that gives each chat its own machine, and in coding agent chats, they work in the same machine and files as the owner, while with other terminals they use their own access to it. #34103
  • Files tab upgrades. With a terminal that reports file changes, the Files tab now updates by itself without a loading spinner when files in the folders it shows change, also through commands run outside the chat. Clicking the path above it lets you type a folder to go to, absolute or relative to the current one, with Tab completing folder names, or select and copy an open file's full path, Markdown files get an Outline button that lists their headings and jumps to the one you pick, and folders in the working directory menu of the message input have an Open folder button that opens them in a new Files tab. #34494, #34525
  • Terminal tab upgrades. Terminal tabs are now named after the title that the program running in them sets, or after the running program itself with Open Terminal 0.17.8 or later on macOS and Linux, and show an icon for well-known programs such as Claude Code, Codex, Python or Node.js. When no terminal is selected for the chat, the menu for opening a new tab still offers Files, new files, terminals, the browser, the desktop and voice notes, and picking one first asks you to choose a terminal from a searchable list.
  • Grouped tools and skills. The Tools and Skills lists in the + menu of the message input are now grouped by where each entry comes from, such as the workspace, tool servers or the terminal. #34085
  • Reply progress on tabs. The chat tab and side chat tabs now show a spinner while a reply is being written, so you can see from another tab when an answer is still coming.
  • Rename from the tab. Double-clicking the chat tab now renames the chat, also a chat someone else made in a folder you own, and on a folder page it renames the folder.
  • Share folders from their menu. The folder menu in the sidebar and on the folder page now has a Share option for administrators and for owners allowed to share folders.
  • Sub-agent permission. Administrators can now limit sub-agents to chosen users and groups with a Sub-agents switch under Features in the default and group permissions, or with "USER_PERMISSIONS_FEATURES_SUBAGENTS", and users without it get neither the sub-agent nor the timer tool. #34040, #34038
  • Lighter coding agent replies. While a coding agent writes its reply, the chat is no longer saved in full about once a second, so long agent chats write several times less to the database for each reply. #34062
  • Labels on failed tool calls. Tool calls that failed now keep the short label the model gave them, also in a group of calls, where one failed call used to hide every label. #34000, #34529
  • Drop files into skills. Files and folders dragged onto a skill's files in the workspace now upload into the open folder, like the upload buttons do.
  • Editable calendars. Calendars can now be renamed and given another color after they are created, from a pencil next to each calendar in the Calendar sidebar. #34136
  • Model names in analytics. Admin analytics now name coding agent models by agent and model for replies made from now on, and the tooltips of the session timeline show model names instead of model IDs.
  • Arena model management. The view filter in Admin Settings > Models now has an Arena Models option that lists only the arena models, and each arena model in Admin Settings > Evaluations has a Clone button that opens a new arena model filled in from it. #34137, #34138
  • OAuth session removals logged. Removing a stored OAuth session because of the "OAUTH_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER" limit, a sign-out sent by the identity provider or a reconnected MCP server now logs a warning naming the user, the session and the reason. #34583, #34580
  • Accessibility improvements. A tab moved with Alt+Shift+Arrow keys now keeps the keyboard focus, so it can be moved several places in a row.
  • General improvements. Various improvements were implemented across the application to enhance performance, stability, and security.
  • Translation updates. Translations for Azerbaijani, Basque, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Cebuano, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Estonian, Faroese, Filipino, Galician, Georgian, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Kabyle, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Malay, Norwegian Bokmål, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish (Spain), Swedish, Tamil, Thai, Tibetan, Turkish, Turkmen, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uyghur and Vietnamese were enhanced and expanded.

Fixed

  • Temporary chats leave no memories. The background memory review now skips temporary chats, so facts from them are no longer saved as memories that show up in later chats. #34263, #34262
  • Whole numbers in parameters. Whole-number fields in the advanced parameters, such as Context Length, Max Tokens and Seed, now reject a value with a decimal point, such as "32.767" typed for 32767, instead of saving it and running the model with a context of only a few tokens. #34416
  • Busy servers with session sharing. With "DATABASE_ENABLE_SESSION_SHARING" on, a burst of page loads no longer stalls for 30 seconds and fails with a "QueuePool limit" error, because chat lists and the inbox no longer open a second database connection for their extra reads. #34185, #34184
  • Uploads during knowledge syncs. With a slow extraction engine, a large knowledge base sync no longer makes every other upload, chat attachments included, wait for an extraction before it is even saved, because files uploaded into knowledge bases now process at most half as many at a time as the server's worker threads ("THREAD_POOL_SIZE"), so other knowledge base uploads may wait their turn during a large sync. #34379
  • Sign-in kept during provider outages. A sign-in provider that is unreachable, rate limited or failing with a server error while a user's token is refreshed no longer deletes that user's stored sign-in, so tools and connections that use the sign-in token work again on the next call instead of only after signing out and back in. #34585, #34578
  • Chat keeps the newest turn. A window that missed a turn, such as a laptop that just woke up, no longer moves the chat back to an older turn when it saves an edited message, so the newest reply stays in the conversation. #34160, #34126
  • Chats with looping history. A chat whose saved messages loop back on themselves now opens and shows its messages instead of freezing the browser tab until it crashes. #34481, #34477
  • Summary kept through compaction. A conversation compacted again between tool calls now keeps what its earlier summary held, and a chat compacted after such a compaction goes on from its newer summary instead of falling back to the older one and sending more than the model can take. #34151, #34141, #34140
  • Steadier context compaction. Compacting a chat by hand right after a failed reply now keeps the summary for the next message instead of losing it along with the failed reply, and automatic compaction now also counts a tool result that ended a reply, such as one too long for the model to answer, so the next message compacts the chat instead of sending it in full. #34434
  • Fewer repeated context lists. With native function calling, the list of available skills and the attached knowledge are no longer added to the chat again before every reply, only when they changed or after compaction, and recalled memories already in the chat are not sent again, so long chats use fewer tokens and need compaction later. #34257
  • Tool call turns without text. Replies in which a model called a tool without writing any text are now sent back to the model without an empty text, so proxies such as LiteLLM no longer turn them into a placeholder line that the model then starts copying into its answers. #34265, #34264
  • Final answers on vLLM. When tool use stops, the request for a final answer no longer ends in a 400 error on vLLM, and Ollama models are kept from calling tools in it. #34176, #34169
  • Ollama proxy tool calls. OpenAI-compatible clients that send back an assistant turn with only tool calls and no text no longer get a 400 "Field required" error from the Ollama OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, so multi-turn tool calling works through it. #34442, #34441
  • Timed-out tool calls explained. A terminal command or tool server call that runs past "AIOHTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_TOOL_SERVER" now reaches the model as a timeout error instead of an empty one, so the model can tell you the call timed out. #34119, #34096
  • Tool calls in summaries. Conversation summaries written with the plain summary prompt, as for models with a filter, now include the tool calls of earlier replies in saved chats. #34139
  • MCP tools reconnect. When an MCP server drops its connection during a reply, for example because it restarted, the next call to one of its tools now connects again instead of every later call in that reply failing with an "MCP client is not connected" error. #34170
  • Large MCP tool lists. MCP servers whose tool list or a single tool result is larger than 1 MB connect and answer again, also through Tether, instead of failing with "Failed to connect to MCP server". #34421, #34201
  • MCP sign-ins with rotating tokens. Two tool calls that refresh the same MCP sign-in at the same time no longer delete the connection with providers that hand out a new refresh token on every refresh, because the refreshes now wait for each other, across workers when Redis is used. #34582
  • MCP OAuth with HS256 tokens. Connecting an MCP server over OAuth 2.1 now works when the server signs its ID token with the client secret, as Readwise does, instead of failing with "Algorithm 'HS256' requires 'oct' key". #34593, #34504
  • MCP OAuth with large headers. Adding an MCP server with OAuth 2.1 and refreshing its tokens now work when its authorization server sends a very large response header, as monday.com does, instead of failing with "Connection error". #34084, #34078
  • Sign-in prompt for SSO tools. When the single sign-on session whose token a tool server forwards has ended, those tools now show as needing a sign-in in the + menu and picking one takes you to sign in again, instead of the tools failing on every call with no hint. #34579
  • OAuth sessions on other devices. Signing in past "OAUTH_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_USER" now removes the stored provider sessions used least recently instead of the ones created first, so a device signed in early and still in use keeps its session, and signing out now removes that browser's stored session unless it is the person's only one for that provider. #34586, #34581
  • Quieter search logs. Knowledge searches and several web search engines no longer write found file names or full search results to the server log at the default level, only with "GLOBAL_LOG_LEVEL" set to "DEBUG". #34146, #34129
  • Deleted accounts leave access lists. Deleting an account now also removes it from the access lists of everything it was given access to, where it used to stay as a row showing only the deleted account's ID. #34223, #30023
  • Local speech-to-text on pip installs. Local speech-to-text in Open WebUI installed with pip now transcribes again instead of failing every recording with an error about "metadata_errors". #34280, #34278
  • OpenAI image generation defaults. Generating images with OpenAI now works with the stock settings, because GPT image models get the auto size instead of the old 512x512 default they reject and Auto can be saved with the model field left empty, and a failed request now shows the provider's own error, such as "Invalid size".
  • Fuller web page text. With the Playwright web loader, the text of definition lists, of figures with their captions and of collapsible sections, open or closed, now reaches the model, so attached web pages and web search results no longer lose content such as the function and parameter descriptions on many documentation sites. #34282, #34281, #34277, #34272
  • Unreachable sites skipped sooner. With SSL verification on, the Playwright, Tavily and Microsoft Web IQ web loaders now skip a site that never answers after 10 seconds instead of waiting about two minutes per link. #34490, #14241
  • Web pages behind internal certificates. With SSL verification on, the Playwright, Tavily and Microsoft Web IQ web loaders now load pages signed by an internal certificate authority set through "AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SSL_CERT_FILE" or "AIOHTTP_CLIENT_SESSION_SSL", and links that spell out a port or a username, instead of rejecting them. #34482, #34479, #34462
  • No keyboard pop-up on phones. On a phone, opening a chat, switching chats or starting a new chat no longer puts the cursor in the message input and brings up the on-screen keyboard over the conversation. #34059
  • Smooth Firefox scrolling. Scrolling up through a long chat in Firefox no longer throws the view back down, sometimes by several screens, while older messages load. #33998, #33994
  • Temporary chat choice kept. With Temporary Chat by default turned on in the interface settings, a new chat switched to a normal chat now stays normal after a page reload.
  • Permission changes reach open pages. When an admin changes permissions, open pages now follow without a reload, so a new chat that is open becomes a temporary chat once Enforce Temporary Chat is turned on instead of failing on the first message, Compare in the model selector turns off and only the first selected model stays once Multiple Models in Chat is turned off, an open channel shows the permission notice in place of the channel once Channels is turned off, and turning off Folders removes Move from the chat menu and closes an open Create Folder window. #34513, #34512, #34515, #34514, #34511, #34510, #34509, #34508, #34507, #34506
  • Images reach coding agents. Images attached to a message in a coding agent chat now reach the agent with the message instead of being dropped without a word. #33993, #33992, #33991
  • Coding agent chat titles. Chats with a coding agent now get a generated title once the agent has replied, instead of keeping the default title. #33971, #33970
  • Agent model switches keep sessions. Switching a coding agent chat to another model of the same agent now resumes the agent's existing session and working folder instead of starting a new session.
  • Readable coding agent errors. When the terminal refuses to start a coding agent, the reply now shows a short error instead of a technical dump containing the whole system prompt. #34173, #34172
  • Sub-agents with browser questions. A sub-agent no longer hangs on "Executing Sub-agent" when a filter or tool asks the browser something, because the script, confirmation or form now appears in the tab that has the chat open. #34045, #34041
  • Sub-agent reports stay together. Two background sub-agent reports that finish close together no longer split the chat into two branches that hide the first report and the reply to it. #34542, #34540
  • Shared chat changes saved. Someone replying in a chat shared with Allow replies can now change its model, terminal and working folder, and the choice is saved to the chat instead of being dropped when it is reopened.
  • Terminal choice kept in folders. In a new chat inside a folder with a default terminal, a terminal you pick or turn off now stays that way when the model changes, instead of going back to the folder default, and a new chat in a folder without a default terminal keeps the terminal you had selected instead of turning it off. #33973
  • Terminal locked during replies. The terminal and working folder pickers in the message input now stay locked while a reply is still being written, so the chat's terminal can no longer be switched in the middle of a reply. #34383
  • Steadier Tether connections. Requests to a computer connected through Tether are no longer cut off after five minutes while data keeps flowing, read-only requests interrupted by a brief disconnect are repeated once Tether reconnects, and a busy computer now refuses new operations right away instead of letting some of them time out.
  • Your devices list updates live. A computer that connects through Tether after the page has loaded now appears under Your devices in the terminal menu right away, and the menu also picks up disconnects and device name changes, instead of needing a page reload.
  • Unsaved terminal file edits kept. An edit not yet saved in a file opened from a terminal's Files tab now comes back with its unsaved mark after you open another chat and return, and a workbook saved while you leave the chat keeps the worksheet you had open. #34135, #34107
  • Long Markdown files. Opening a long Markdown file from a terminal's Files, or typing in one of its code blocks, no longer freezes the page for many seconds, because code blocks without a known language now show as plain text instead of being checked against every language, which also keeps notes and the rich text message input responsive. #34491, #34486
  • File cards follow the terminal. A file shown inline in a reply now gets its preview, Download and Open back as soon as its terminal is picked again, and stops reaching the file once another terminal is picked, instead of keeping its first state until a page reload. #34101
  • Working folder stays put. Browsing to another folder in a Files tab no longer changes the working folder shown in the working directory menu and used by a new chat, and opening Files again shows an existing Files tab where you left it instead of moving it to the working folder.
  • Terminal skill mentions after reload. A sent message that mentions a skill of the picked terminal now still shows it as a chip after a page reload, and the + menu lists that terminal's skills right away, instead of both only working after the skill list was opened once. #34102
  • File sizes after Refresh. In a terminal's file viewer, Refresh and the back and forward arrows now keep the open file's real size instead of showing 0 B, and Refresh shows the new size when the file changed. #34459, #34458
  • Files menu near edges. The menu from a right click on the empty part of a Files list now opens upwards or to the left when there is no room below or beside the pointer, so all of its entries stay inside the window. #34125, #34097
  • Local embedding model folders. With the embedding model set to a folder on disk, saving Admin Settings > Documents no longer shows a "Model filesystem path detected" error and now also saves the embedding settings such as the batch size, which were skipped before. #33978, #33977
  • PowerPoint decks with sections. PowerPoint files that use sections now preview in the chat and the knowledge base file viewer and show their comments, instead of failing with "Missing slide relationship". #34276, #34270
  • Large workbook sheets. Excel workbooks with a sheet too large to preview now still open with their sheet tabs in a terminal's Files tab, the chat and the knowledge base, where that sheet says it is too large to preview and can be downloaded, instead of the whole file failing to preview. #34247
  • Notes with footnotes. Notes containing footnote references such as "[^1]" now open and show their content instead of failing with an error. #33987, #33986
  • Note recordings on S3 storage. Recordings made in a note now upload to S3-compatible storage that rejects colons in file names and are named like "Recording-2026-11-16 15-25-06.webm" in every language, instead of after a date that slashes could cut short. #34545, #34543
  • Optional valves set to Custom. Switching an optional valve, such as an on/off setting, from Default to Custom in the Valves section of the chat controls no longer fails with "Error updating function user valves", and emptying an optional on/off or number valve sets it back to its default. #34478, #34475
  • Math in table headers. Formulas in table headers now keep their letters as written instead of being capitalized along with the header text. #34245, #34238
  • Math next to hyphens. Inline formulas written directly next to a hyphen or non-breaking hyphen, as some models write them, now render instead of staying plain text or showing a math error. #34244, #34237
  • Pinning keeps chat order. Pinning, unpinning, archiving or restoring a chat no longer moves it to the top of the chat list as if it had just been updated, and pinning a chat or moving it to a folder no longer marks it as read.
  • Drafts kept per folder. Unsent text in a new chat now stays with the folder or home page you typed it on, so opening another folder shows that folder's own unsent text instead of bringing yours along.
  • Links in messages. A link to a folder in a chat or channel message now opens the folder in Open WebUI instead of a new browser tab, and Ctrl or Cmd clicking a link to a chat, note or channel in a message now opens it in a new browser tab instead of the current one. #34464
  • Tagging chats in parallel. Adding the same new tag to several chats at the same time, as an API client tagging a batch of chats or two chat imports can do, no longer fails with a server error for all but one chat and leaves the others untagged. #34144, #34143
  • Thread reply notifications. Clicking the browser notification for a reply in a channel thread now opens that thread instead of the channel with the thread closed. #34233, #34232
  • Side chats after reload. A saved side chat tab restored after a page reload or on another device now shows only the side conversation again, instead of also listing the messages copied from the parent chat. #34002
  • Browser tab in two windows. With the same chat open in two windows, a Browser tab in Chrome mode no longer keeps reconnecting in both, and the window that lost the tab shows that the browser opened in another viewer. #34133, #34095
  • Ports open in new tabs. The Open in new tab button beside a port on the start page of a Browser tab now opens the server running on that port instead of a "404: Not Found" page. #34120, #34108
  • Smooth Browser tab resizing. Dragging the divider of the side panel no longer makes the Browser tab flicker and resize the page in slow motion. #33989, #33988
  • Terminal proxy headers. A "TERMINAL_PROXY_HEADERS" entry written in a different letter case now replaces the terminal's own header instead of being sent next to it, and repeated headers from the terminal such as several cookies are all passed on. #34092
  • Groups need a name. A new group can no longer be saved without a name from a tab other than General, because Save stays off until a name is typed and the server now rejects empty or blank group names. #34518
  • User list API groups. The admin endpoint that lists all users now includes each user's groups instead of an empty list. #34489, #26156
  • Model filter tags update. The tag filter of the model selector now also lists tags that models gain while a chat is open, instead of only the tags present when the page loaded. #33990, #33806
  • Mark folder chats read. Mark all as read in the menu on a folder page now marks the folder's chats as read instead of doing nothing. #34404, #34403
  • Folder page kept. Opening a chat in another browser tab no longer sends a folder's chat list back to page 1. #34145, #34142
  • Same-folder chat drops. Dropping a chat back on the folder it is already in no longer moves it there again and reloads every folder in the sidebar. #34461, #34460
  • Comment box on Android. Writing a comment on selected text on an Android phone no longer closes the comment box as soon as the keyboard opens.
  • Steadier menu placement. Menus that open above their button, such as Model controls and the + menu of the message input, now grow upward when their content changes instead of briefly covering the message input, and right-aligned menus in Firefox no longer creep sideways while they open. #34052, #34051, #34227, #34226
  • Long settings text boxes. Long prompt templates and JSON fields in Admin Settings now stop growing at a set height and scroll, instead of stretching the page to fit all of their text. #34569
  • Hover preview behind menus. A chat's hover preview in the sidebar no longer opens on top of another chat's open menu and covers its items. #34231, #34230
  • Hover preview without bubbles. With Chat Bubble UI turned off, your messages in a chat's hover preview now show as padded bubbles instead of text squeezed onto a grey block. #34347
  • Translated automation schedules. The Schedule button in the dialog that creates an automation now shows the schedule in the chosen language instead of always in English. #34428, #34426
  • Qdrant version warning. Connecting to a Qdrant 1.20 server, as the vector database or for external Qdrant knowledge bases, no longer logs a client version warning, which servers on Qdrant 1.18 or older now get instead. #34485, #34483
  • Image zoom reset. Resetting the zoom of an image preview from below 10% now returns it to 100% and centers it again. #34080, #34079
  • Steady Tools count. The count on the Tools tab of the workspace no longer drops to 0 for a moment when the Tools page opens. #34236
  • Unpin tooltip on notes. The Unpin button on a pinned note in the sidebar now shows a tooltip, as it does on pinned models. #34568, #34567

Changed

  • Terminals 0.4.0 required. Connections to a Terminals server no longer carry a policy in Admin Settings > Integrations, so the Policy ID, image, resource, storage, idle timeout and Terminal Contexts settings and the Refresh Terminals button are gone, the server has to run Terminals 0.4.0 or later, and models, folders, automations and chats that used the old connection need one of the new terminals selected. Upgrading Terminals from 0.3.x takes its manual migration, as there is no automatic one, new Terminals installations start without a template, Open WebUI now connects with the Terminals server key, and "TERMINALS_OPEN_WEBUI_URL" and "TERMINALS_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL" should be removed from the Terminals settings. Open Terminal and Tether terminal connections are not affected.
  • Direct connections move to Tether. Settings > Connections and Settings > Tools are gone together with the Direct Connections and Direct Integrations switches in Admin Settings, the Direct Tool Servers permission and the "ENABLE_DIRECT_CONNECTIONS", "ENABLE_DIRECT_INTEGRATIONS" and "USER_PERMISSIONS_FEATURES_DIRECT_TOOL_SERVERS" settings, so models, tool servers and terminals that users added in their own settings no longer appear. Users add them in the Tether app (0.1.14 or later, 0.1.16 for MCP servers) instead, where they stay on their own computer and work in every Open WebUI they connect.
  • Image settings become connections. On the first start of this version, the image generation and editing settings are turned into image connections that everyone who could use them before keeps using, and from then on the image environment variables such as "IMAGE_GENERATION_ENGINE", "IMAGES_OPENAI_API_BASE_URL" and "COMFYUI_BASE_URL" are no longer read unless "ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG" is turned off.
  • Locked Docker dependencies. The standard and slim Docker images now install every Python package except PyTorch from lock files pinned with hashes, so rebuilding the same version installs the same packages, and custom images that edit "backend/requirements.txt" must regenerate the locks with "backend/update-locks.sh" for the edit to take effect. #33981, #33979
  • New coding agent model IDs. Coding agent models now get IDs made only of letters, digits, dashes and underscores, which makes pinned Cursor and Pi models work, and pins, default models and automations that point at an agent model whose name had other characters, dots included as in most Codex models, need the model picked again. #34171, #34168
  • Coding agent sessions restart once. The first new message in a coding agent chat from an earlier version starts a new agent session that gets the chat so far as text, instead of resuming the agent's own session.
  • Image API model checks. Image generation and edit requests sent through the API now run on the model they name, which has to be one of the caller's image models or the request fails with an error, instead of image generation ignoring the named model.
  • Live update events renamed. Real-time updates for notes, comments, the inbox, access changes, encrypted channels and channel app errors now arrive as typed messages on the main "events" socket channel, so custom clients that listened for the old event names such as "events:note" or "note:presence" need to listen there instead.
  • Chat write access field. Chat responses from the API now carry the saved sharing mode in "share_mode" and report whether you can reply in a new "write_access" field, so custom clients that read "share_mode" for that need to switch.
  • Terminal uploads go to files. New terminal connections now start with Chat Uploads set to Filesystem and computers connected through Tether always use it, so files attached in a chat are saved into the selected terminal's working folder instead of being processed as regular chat uploads, while existing connections keep their setting. Open Terminal 0.17.20 or later is recommended, as it fixes uploads becoming unreadable in multi-user setups.
  • Chat menu items moved. Overview, Artifacts and Comments are no longer in the chat's menu and now open from the + menu of the tab bar, where Overview opens as a tab beside the chat instead of a full-screen window.
  • Note comments button. Comments on a note now open from a button in the note's top bar instead of from its menu, and in a note you can edit, commenting on selected text is now a Comment button in the formatting toolbar.
  • One heading menu. The formatting toolbar of the message input and of notes now offers Heading 1, 2 and 3 in a single heading menu instead of three separate buttons.
  • Attachments menu renamed. The Add Context entry in the + menu of the message input, which holds the options to attach web pages, files, notes, knowledge and chats, is now called Attachments. #34431
  • Capabilities now Features. The Capabilities section of the model editor is now called Features. #34433
  • Knowledge base labels. The knowledge picker in the chat, the knowledge selector of the model editor and attached knowledge bases now call them Knowledge or Knowledge Base instead of Collection, the vector database term, and the search box inside a knowledge base now says Search Files. #34432

entry.title: v0.13.3
entry.content:
Added

  • 🦾 Agents in automations. The automation editor now lets you choose a terminal and working folder, then select a coding agent available there. Scheduled runs use that saved terminal and folder, and check that the terminal and agent are still available before starting. Agent automations send their results to a chat; channel destinations remain available for ordinary models. Commit
  • 📂 Change terminal and folder during a chat. You can now choose a different terminal or working folder after sending messages, including in temporary chats. Both controls remain disabled while a reply is being generated. Commit
  • 🇧🇷 Brazilian Portuguese translations. Added missing translations for terminal and folder controls, Git actions, spreadsheet editing, voice notes, tab shortcuts, notification sounds and tool settings. Updated the explanations for document retrieval, tool permissions and voice settings. #33945

Fixed

  • 📂 Files tabs follow terminal changes. Switching a chat to another terminal now updates its open Files tabs to show that terminal's files, instead of leaving the previous terminal's folders on screen. With a terminal set to "Per chat", the Files tab also switches to the chat's own files after the first message. #33954
  • 🧭 Agents in unsupported model pickers. Connecting a terminal no longer adds its coding agents to Admin Models, base-model selectors, Arena candidates, task-model settings, group defaults, sub-agent settings, channel mentions or the Playground. Notes also stop choosing a terminal agent for title generation. Agents cannot be saved or imported as custom models or their base models, and their chat menu no longer offers Edit. Commit, Commit
  • 🔌 Agent list after switching terminals. Changing terminals immediately removes the previous terminal's agents from the chat's model list while the new list loads. A model-list request from a chat you have left can no longer replace the current list. Commit
  • 📋 Copy buttons over plain HTTP. At a plain HTTP address on your local network, copying comment links, search links, shared-chat links, webhook URLs, chat IDs, Git branch names, commit hashes and spreadsheet cells now works. Copy Formatted Text preserves formatting, and copied text keeps its final line break. #33939
  • 📝 Clipboard prompts and Auto-Copy Response over plain HTTP. Prompts using the clipboard placeholder now insert into chats and channels even when the browser blocks clipboard access, with a message explaining that the clipboard could not be read. Auto-Copy Response stays off and shows a permission message instead of silently failing to turn on; turning it off no longer requires clipboard access. #33939
  • 🧠 DeepSeek thinking mode with skills, knowledge and memories. These chats no longer fail with a missing reasoning error when the connection's Provider is set to "llama.cpp". DeepSeek thinking mode still requires that setting; connections using "Default" are unchanged. #33950
  • 🏷️ Labels on grouped tool calls. With Tool Call Labels enabled, a group of tool calls keeps the labels that are present even if one call has none. The unlabeled call shows its tool name instead of making the whole group lose its labels. #33932
  • 💬 Tool labels in later replies. The model now sees the labels it wrote for earlier tool calls when continuing a reply or answering another message, removing a reason it could stop writing labels as the conversation continued. #33953
  • 🔎 Knowledge searches containing punctuation. Searches in knowledge files now find text such as "Art. 40" when the model marks the period as literal punctuation, instead of returning no matches. #33936
  • 🪟 Side Chat with Temporary Chat disabled. Leaving Enforce Temporary Chat switched on while disabling Temporary Chat no longer prevents users from sending and saving side chats or dragging an existing chat into the side panel. #33930
  • 🏠 Home folder tab title. A Files tab at the connected machine's home directory now says "Home" instead of showing the directory name, including when reopening saved tabs. Other folders keep their names. Commit
  • 🦙 Missing Ollama in Docker images. Building the image that includes Ollama now fails if Ollama was not installed, instead of producing an image that cannot start Ollama after its download failed. #33944
  • 📄 Errors after leaving a chat. Closing or leaving a chat while its tab layout is being saved no longer fills the server log with an error report for the dropped connection. #33929

Fixed

  • 🔓 Chat over plain HTTP. Opening Open WebUI over plain HTTP at a LAN or Docker address now loads new and existing chats instead of staying on a spinner with "crypto.randomUUID is not a function". #33919
  • 📝 Comments and Markdown editing over plain HTTP. Creating, replying to and editing comments, and editing Markdown files containing rendered blocks such as Mermaid diagrams or callouts, no longer fail with the same UUID error. Commit

entry.title: v0.13.1
entry.content:
Added

  • 🦾 Coding agents as models. On an Open Terminal that offers agents, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi now appear in the model picker. You can chat with them or call them by voice, choose their reasoning effort and service tier, and approve their tool requests in the chat. Each conversation uses one agent, and agent chats cannot be regenerated, continued or edited and resent. If an agent's terminal goes away, its chats and new chats fall back to the default model and earlier replies keep the agent's name. Autocompletion in agent chats uses the task model, or is skipped when there is none. #33843, #33860, #33880, #33857
  • 🪢 Introducing Tether. Tether is the new desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that ties your own computer to Open WebUI. Sign in once and your computer shows up under Your devices in the terminal menu, so models, coding agents and automations can work in your real files, repositories and tools, and you can reach them from any browser, including your phone. Tether connects out to Open WebUI, so there are no ports to open, its terminal output resumes after a dropped connection, and it delivers notifications to your desktop even when no Open WebUI page is open. It signs in with a renewable session that expires after 90 days without use by default, set with "SESSION_EXPIRES_IN".
  • 💸 Much cheaper tool chats. Chats that use tools now cost much less. Citation instructions, memory recall, the skills list and attached knowledge are no longer rewritten into the system prompt or your message on every tool round, so the start of the conversation stays the same between requests and providers can serve it from their prompt cache. Custom pipes see a different message layout as a result; see Context as hidden tool results under Changed. #33852
  • 🚦 Auto tool permissions. Administrators can now turn on Auto, a third tool permission mode next to Full access and Ask for approval (off by default). A review model checks each tool call and runs it right away only when it judges that no confirmation is needed. The review sends the tool, its arguments and your last few messages to the configured scoring API, and any call it cannot review, because of an error, a timeout or too much context, asks for approval.
  • 📚 Full text for small files. Files whose extracted text is shorter than a new threshold (50,000 characters by default, set with "RAG_FULL_TEXT_CHAR_THRESHOLD" or in the admin Documents settings) are now included in full instead of through retrieval. This applies both when Preload files adds the content to the conversation and when the model reads an attached file with its file search tool, and the file viewer shows when it happens.
  • ⏱️ Faster large chats. Large chats now open about twice as fast, and marking a chat as read or unread or removing a tag from it is 4 to 6 times faster. #33665, #33666
  • 🏎️ Faster chat access checks. Sending messages, typing indicators, shared links, comments and file access no longer load the whole conversation just to check who may access it, which helps most on large chats. #33667, #33669
  • 🔧 More forgiving tool calls. Tool calls with arguments wrapped in code fences, encoded twice or sent as text instead of numbers and booleans now run, and tool calls a model writes out as plain text markup are recognised and executed. #33868
  • 🛑 Tool loop stops. A tool call that fails twice in a row with the same arguments now ends the tool loop so the model writes a final answer, and a reply cut off by the token limit no longer runs its unfinished tool calls.
  • 🛠️ Default tools for models. The Model Defaults section in the admin Models settings now has a Tools picker, models without their own tool list start new chats with those tools enabled, and the new model form preselects them. #33749, #33787
  • 🚀 Faster channels. The channel list, the channel messages and the replied-to messages in a channel now load much faster, especially with many channels or many replies, and new database indexes speed up channel threads and reactions. #33690, #33691, #33688
  • 🪶 Lighter reasoning streams. Long reasoning replies from providers such as OpenRouter now send far less data to the browser and to Redis while they stream. #33698
  • 🗂️ Faster sidebar chat list. The chat list in the sidebar now appears as soon as its own data is ready instead of waiting for the channel list. #33686
  • ⌨️ Faster typing after large pastes. Typing in the chat input after pasting 16,000 lines of text is now about 117 times faster, down from 8.6 seconds to 74 milliseconds per keystroke. #33729, #12087
  • 🧮 Faster Redis filter lookups. With Redis enabled, chat requests now look up the filters of a model faster. #33668
  • 🪟 Split tab panes. On large screens, dragging a tab or a chat to the edge of the workspace, or pressing the new Split screen button, splits it into resizable panes, so several tabs, including the chat, stay visible side by side. Tabs can also be reordered and moved between panes with a long press and drag on touch screens. Commit
  • 🧳 Tabs remembered per chat. The open tabs, split layout and selected terminal of each chat are now saved privately for each user on the server and restored when you reopen the chat, even on another device. Signing out warns you about unsaved file edits. #33899, #33885
  • 🪣 Batched Tool Search calls. With Tool Search on, the model can run several independent tools it found in a single call_tool request, which saves model turns and so lowers the cost of tool-heavy chats.
  • 🧭 Tool Search engines. Tool Search in the admin Interface settings can now match tools with embeddings from the Documents embedding model (kept in memory, not stored) or by sending the query and tool definitions to a relevance-scoring API, besides the default keyword search.
  • 🏷️ Readable tool call labels. Administrators can now turn on Tool Call Labels in Admin Settings > Interface or with "ENABLE_TOOL_CALL_LABELS", off by default, to ask the model for short descriptions in the user's language of what each tool call is doing and what it did. Commit
  • ✂️ Chat read limit. Admins can limit how much of an earlier chat the Chat History tools return, with "VIEW_CHAT_MAX_CHARS" or the new Chat Read Limit field in Admin Settings > General, and the newest messages are kept while older ones are cut. #33695, #33608
  • 🌍 Client IP header placeholders. Custom headers of connections can now use "{{USER_IP}}" and "{{X_FORWARDED_FOR}}" to pass the client address on to the upstream provider, and both are empty for automations and background jobs. #33833, #33819
  • ✉️ Non-ASCII email addresses. The sign-up page and the add and edit user dialogs now accept email addresses with non-ASCII characters. #33693, #33681
  • 🕒 Reply finish time. Assistant replies now show the time they finished instead of the time the prompt was sent. #33895
  • 🧐 Channel message search. Each channel header has a Search button that searches the messages of that channel.
  • 🔔 Notifications open their chat. Clicking a desktop notification now brings Open WebUI to the front and opens the related chat, channel or calendar.
  • 📮 MCP Apps message the chat. An MCP App can now send a text message to the chat, which you confirm first in a Confirm Prompt from Embed dialog. #33907
  • 🖱️ Drag chats into side panel. Dragging a chat from the sidebar onto the chat area opens it as a side chat tab, and a side chat can now also be started from an empty new chat.
  • 🪄 Quick open files. A new shortcut, Cmd+P (Ctrl+P elsewhere), opens a search box that finds files in the selected terminal by name or path and opens the one you pick in a tab.
  • 🎹 Tab keyboard shortcuts. New shortcuts, which can be changed in Settings > Keyboard, open the Files, Desktop, Comments, new chat, new file, new terminal and new browser tabs, close and switch between tabs and toggle the split screen.
  • 🗺️ Working directory picker. The message input has a working directory menu with folder search, a Recently Used list kept per user on the terminal and an Open Folder dialog.
  • 📂 Folder default terminal. A folder can now have a default terminal and working directory in its Advanced settings, used for new chats in that folder.
  • 🧾 Editable spreadsheets. Excel files in the file view can now be edited in the preview, with a formula bar, pasting from other spreadsheets and resizable columns, and saved back to the file, while formula cells and protected sheets stay read-only.
  • 🖋️ Markdown and code editing. Markdown files in the file view now open in a rich text editor that saves back to Markdown, where pasted or dropped images are uploaded to the terminal, and the code editor suggests words that already appear in the file. Other text files and the Source view of previews now use the code editor directly, without a separate Edit step. Commit
  • 🌳 Clone Git repositories. The file browser and the folder pickers can now clone a Git repository from an HTTP(S) or SSH URL into the chosen folder of the selected terminal.
  • 🧬 Git changes in the editor. The code editor now marks the lines of a file that were added or changed since the last commit.
  • 🔖 File browser Git status. Files and folders in the file browser are marked with a Git status letter such as M, A, D or U, and folders show that they contain changes.
  • 🌿 Git panel feedback and resizing. The Git panel now shows what it is doing, such as staging, pushing or fetching, and its file list can be resized.
  • 🧹 Discard any Git change. The Git panel can now discard staged and new files too, and its confirmation warns that files not in the last commit are deleted and that this cannot be undone.
  • 🧲 Drag files into chat. Files from the terminal file browser can be dragged, one or several at once, into the message input to attach them, also with a long press on touch screens.
  • 🗃️ Multiple Files tabs. The + menu can now open several Files tabs for the same terminal, each with its own folder and the folder name as its tab title, and moving files refreshes the other Files tabs on that terminal. Commit
  • 🔲 Drag to select files. Several files in the file browser can now be selected by dragging a selection box over them.
  • 🪂 Spring-loaded Files tabs. Holding a dragged file over a Files tab for half a second switches to that tab, so files can be moved into folders of another tab.
  • ⚡ Faster terminal rendering. The terminal tab now renders with WebGL where the browser supports it and takes in bursts of output in larger batches, so heavy output is handled faster.
  • 🩺 Terminal system info. The terminal menu now has a System info view with the terminal's CPU, memory, disk, network, uptime and top processes.
  • 🖌️ Edit images from the terminal. The image edit tool can now take source images from the selected terminal by file path, as PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF up to 25 megapixels. #33824
  • 🎙️ Voice notes in files. A new shortcut, Cmd+Alt+M (Ctrl+Alt+M elsewhere), records a voice note, can transcribe it, and saves the recording with a Markdown note in the current folder of the selected terminal, then opens the note in a tab. Escape cancels a recording. #33902, #33903
  • 📢 Model availability events. Open WebUI now publishes model.available and model.unavailable events when a model appears in or disappears from the fetched model list.
  • 🗒️ Descriptions in model pickers. The tool, skill, filter, action and sub-agent pickers in the model editor now show each item's description under its name. #33723
  • 🔢 Grouped token counts. Whole numbers in the token usage tooltip are now grouped by thousands for the interface language, for example 26,678,623. #33896
  • 🎼 Notification sound styles. The notification sound setting now offers Chime, Soft, Bell and Tap sounds, with a play button to preview each one.
  • 🔄 General improvements. Various improvements were implemented across the application to enhance performance, stability, and security.
  • 🌐 Translation updates. Translations for Portuguese (Brazil), Azerbaijani, Basque, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Cebuano, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Estonian, Faroese, Filipino, Galician, Georgian, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Irish, Japanese, Kabyle, Korean, Lithuanian, Malay, Norwegian Bokmål, Persian, Polish, Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish (Spain), Swedish, Tamil, Thai, Tibetan, Turkish, Turkmen, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uyghur and Vietnamese were enhanced and expanded.

Fixed

  • 🛡️ Security Advisory: This release contains security fixes. We strongly recommend updating all deployments as soon as possible to have the latest security fixes in place. These fixes are not listed in this changelog; we will publish the security advisories for them immediately following CVE assignment. Advisories
  • 🗄️ Redis Cluster chats. Sending a chat message on a Redis Cluster deployment no longer fails while the personal terminal relay starts. #33766
  • 🚪 Automatic SSO sign-in. With automatic SSO redirect on, an expired session now signs you back in without a state mismatch error. #33791, #33783
  • 🎨 OpenAI image default model. Image generation with the OpenAI engine now defaults to GPT-IMAGE 2 instead of the shut-down DALL·E 2, and the shut-down DALL·E models are no longer offered. #33694, #33578
  • 🖼️ Default GPT image requests. OpenAI image generation and editing with no model explicitly set no longer send an unsupported response format to the default GPT image model. #33875
  • 🔐 Terminal Session authentication. Terminal connections set to Session authentication now accept an API key, so Verify Connection, the policy settings and the terminal tools work again. #33699, #30001, #33579
  • 🦙 Ollama broken tool calls. Chats with Ollama models no longer get stuck after a tool call with cut-off, rejected or empty arguments. #33697, #33671
  • 🧠 Complete compaction summaries. Context compaction summaries are no longer cut off at 1000 tokens, which could leave reasoning models with an empty or truncated summary. #33726
  • 💾 Prompt cache on tool results. Tool results sent through OpenAI-compatible gateways now keep their prompt cache marker, so Anthropic models behind OpenRouter or LiteLLM can cache the prefix in tool loops. #33757, #33755
  • 📖 File read size limit. Reading a file by line range now stops at the same size limit as other reads, so one read can no longer overflow the context window of the model. #33696, #33607
  • 🧰 Tool Search retries. A malformed tool call with Tool Search on no longer disables tools for the rest of the reply, so the model can correct its arguments and try again. #33872
  • 🧩 Split tool calls. When a model sends several tool calls glued into one, the chat no longer shows an extra tool call that never gets a result. #33779, #33778
  • 🔎 External knowledge base queries. External knowledge bases now search with every generated query at the same time instead of using only the results of the first one. #33704, #33184
  • 📊 Large spreadsheet uploads. Uploading a large, sparsely filled spreadsheet no longer takes minutes and stalls the server. #33770, #33768
  • 🧱 Milvus knowledge base uploads. Adding a file to a knowledge base on Milvus no longer processes the file a second time or stores its chunks twice. #33745, #33744
  • 📄 MinerU 4.1 servers. The MinerU document loader in local mode now works with MinerU 4.1 servers, where every document used to fail. #33719, #33718
  • 🔑 MCP OAuth stays signed in. The login to an MCP tool server that uses OAuth is no longer lost when the provider has a temporary outage while the token is refreshed. #33805, #33803
  • 📍 Location lookup delays. With location access turned on, sending a message no longer waits for a slow or unanswered browser location request.
  • 🗓️ Automation schedule examples. Models creating automations through the built-in tool no longer hit "Invalid RRULE" errors caused by a wrong example schedule format. #33732, #33730
  • ♿ Keyboard and screen reader fixes. Keyboard focus now stays where it belongs: on buttons while they save, in place when you cancel a message edit, switch message versions or sort and page a workspace or notes list, on the first and last page buttons, and in the title field while a note title is generated. Closing a channel thread, a note panel or a chat menu returns focus to where it was, and the sign-in skip link moves focus to the form. The show password button is now wide enough to hit, and holding Shift no longer swaps row buttons for Delete while a keyboard user has focus.
  • 🕵️ Audit log secret masking. With request auditing on, the audit log now masks API keys, tokens and secrets saved in the admin settings, not only passwords. #33746
  • 🔇 Queries kept out of logs. The default server log no longer contains your search queries or the provider address of a failing external reranker. #33701
  • 💬 Chat message search. Workspace search now finds message text and shows matching excerpts in chats whose messages are stored separately from the chat record. Commit
  • 🔃 Search results stay current. Notes, archived and shared chats, the admin user list and the knowledge and file pickers in the message input no longer let an older search replace the results of a newer one. Commit
  • 👎 Feedback details saved. A thumbs-down reason and comment are no longer lost when saved before the feedback tags finish generating. #33716
  • 🎒 Side chat default tools. New side chats now start with the same default tools, skills, filters and web search as a normal chat with that model. #33788
  • ✅ Side chat tool approvals. Tool calls in side chats now show working approval controls and resume the reply after approval. #33889
  • ❓ Side chat questions. Questions asked through the model's ask_user tool now appear in side chats and can be answered or dismissed, including after reopening the chat. #33901
  • ⏩ Continued replies on Responses connections. Continuing a reply on a Responses API connection now adds the new text to the existing reply.
  • 🛂 Model required before sending. The file ask box, follow-up suggestions and queued messages now report "Model not selected" instead of trying to send when no model is selected. #33838
  • 👻 Temporary chat button with tabs. The Temporary Chat button is back on new chats when the tabbed layout is on. #33680
  • 🪧 Stable MCP app views. MCP apps in chat no longer reload and lose their state while the message around them updates.
  • 🎴 Artifacts keep the chat visible. Opening an HTML or SVG preview from a reply now uses the side pane instead of replacing the visible chat tab. #33894
  • 📣 Banners in tabbed view. Admin banners and license notices now show on the new chat page when the terminal tabs split the screen. #33789
  • 📡 Tabs over plain HTTP. The New File, New Terminal and Browser tabs in the side panel now open when Open WebUI is reached over plain HTTP on a LAN or Docker address. #33847, #33845
  • 🕶️ Per-chat terminals in temporary chats. Per-chat workspace terminals are no longer offered in temporary chats, where sending to them failed, and one already selected is deselected when Temporary mode is turned on. #33866, #33861
  • 🖥️ Terminal kept on model switch. Switching to a model without its own default terminal no longer turns off the terminal selected in the chat.
  • 📁 Working folder in new chats. The terminal working folder of a new chat is no longer reset to the root when the chat is created before the file browser has finished loading.
  • 📞 Return to call. The Return to call button now reopens the active voice call after switching to the chat tab. #33898
  • 🔕 Channel notifications clear on read. Opening a channel now marks its notifications as read.
  • 🪝 Webhooks window stability. The channel Webhooks window no longer jumps back to the webhook list when a new message arrives, so edits in progress are kept. #33776, #33775
  • 🎧 Background audio on iOS. With Auto-Playback Response off, tapping in Open WebUI or opening a chat no longer stops audio playing in other apps on iOS. #33780
  • 🖨️ Scanned PDF preview. PDF previews no longer show blank pages for scanned PDFs that store their pages as JPEG2000 images. #33906, #33905
  • 🔬 Preview zoom stability. Zooming in PDF, Word and PowerPoint previews no longer resets or drifts when you switch tabs, change slides or resize the pane. #33836, #33835
  • 📌 File preview from Controls. A file preview opened from the Controls menu no longer closes when you click inside it. #33831, #33828
  • 🔭 Tab bar and UI scale. Tab content no longer slides under the tab bar when the UI scale is above 1. #33830, #33829
  • 🔘 Desktop app top clicks. In the desktop app, banners and menus near the top of the window now take clicks instead of dragging the window.
  • 📱 Mobile menu keyboard. Closing the + menu on a phone no longer opens the keyboard. #33893
  • 📝 File rename in terminal. Renaming a file or folder in the Open Terminal file browser no longer shows a false error after the rename succeeded. #33786
  • 📋 Stable file selection. Selecting files no longer shifts the file rows when the bulk action bar appears, and clicking an empty area of the file list clears the selection. Commit
  • 🫥 Selection popups on scroll. Scrolling the file view dismisses its Ask box, and scrolling a rich text editor dismisses its floating formatting menus until the selection changes. Commit, Commit
  • 🙈 Empty control groups hidden. When every control of a group is hidden with Visible controls, the empty group heading or submenu no longer shows. #33867
  • 🌄 Chat background behind tabs. The chat tab bar no longer covers the chat background with a solid strip. #33849
  • 🌫️ Top bar blur. The top bars of Workspace, Admin Panel, Playground and Calendar no longer blur a page background image. #33799, #33798
  • 🗑️ Feedback model filter. Deleting the last feedback of a model in the Evaluations feedback list now clears the model filter. #33794, #33793
  • 🔤 Visible controls labels. Six toggles under Visible controls in the Admin Interface settings now show their names instead of raw translation keys. #33734
  • 🤫 Quiet terminal disconnects. Closing the file panel or a terminal view right after opening it no longer logs an error traceback on the server. #33863, #33850
  • 📜 Quieter MCP connection logs. Logs no longer fill with a warning for every MCP server a user has not connected yet each time they load Open WebUI. #33663
  • 🪪 OAuth token refresh warnings. Refreshing OAuth tokens with a client secret no longer logs deprecation warnings on every call. #33700, #33297

Changed

  • ⚠️ Database Migrations: This release includes database schema changes; we strongly recommend backing up your database and all associated data before upgrading in production environments. If you are running a multi-worker, multi-server, or load-balanced deployment, all instances must be updated simultaneously, rolling updates are not supported and will cause application failures due to schema incompatibility.
  • 💥 Preload files off by default. With native function calling, the default, attached files are no longer added to the conversation automatically, and models read them with their file tools instead. Models without tool support or without the Files built-in tool can no longer see attached files until you turn on Preload files in the model's Capabilities. Legacy function calling, and API requests that do not come from a chat in the web UI, keep the old behavior. #33815
  • 🎯 Retrieval defaults. Unless you saved your own values, "RAG_TOP_K" and "RAG_TOP_K_RERANKER" now default to 10 instead of 3, and "CHUNK_SIZE" to 1024 instead of 1000. Each query now retrieves more text, so prompts with knowledge get longer. The new chunk size applies to files processed from now on; existing knowledge keeps its chunks until it is reindexed.
  • 🧷 Context as hidden tool results. With native function calling, memory recall, the skills list and the attached knowledge list now arrive as hidden tool results after your message instead of in the system prompt. This is what keeps tool chats cacheable, and it means custom pipes can see a tool message as the last message.
  • 🗨️ Side chats are saved. Side chats, which were always temporary in 0.13.0, are now saved as regular chats and appear in the chat list. They stay temporary only when you turn on Temporary Chat in the side chat or your admin enforces temporary chats.
  • 🚧 Tool call limit. Reaching the tool call limit now makes the model write a final answer without tools, instead of ending the reply with the "Tool-call limit reached" error.
  • 🔦 Tool Search prompt. With Tool Search on, the model no longer sees a list of the hidden tools and finds them only by searching.
  • ✏️ Always Use Full Text. The Full Context Mode setting in the admin Documents settings is now called Always Use Full Text and includes complete documents regardless of the full text threshold.
  • ↔️ Always full-width tabs. On large screens the tabbed workspace now always fills the chat area, with the chat as one of its tabs, and the full-width toggle added in 0.13.0 is gone.
  • 🔀 Integrations moved into + menu. The Integrations button is now part of the + menu in the message input, and the new Show Input Selections setting, off by default, controls whether selected tools, skills, filters and capabilities are shown beside it.
  • 🔓 Side chat permission. The Allow Side Chat permission no longer requires the Temporary Chat permission.
  • 🕸️ Chrome first in Browser tab. The Browser tab now starts in Chrome mode when the terminal offers it, and switches to Proxy mode with a message if Chrome fails to start.
  • ⛔ Terminal select setting removed. The Show Files on Terminal Select setting has been removed from the Interface settings. #33855, #33840

entry.title: v0.13.0
entry.content:
Added

  • 📑 Tabbed workspace. The Tabs button at the top of a chat now opens a workspace for files, multiple terminal sessions, artifacts, previews, voice calls and comments. Add tabs from the + menu, drag to reorder them, and create and save new files directly into the selected terminal. Keep the conversation and its working files together while coding, analyzing data or reviewing generated documents. Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit
  • 🖥️ Open Terminal Desktop tab for computer use. Open the Desktop tab from the + menu to view and control the desktop provided by your connected Open Terminal, with mouse, keyboard, clipboard and audio support where available. With a model that can call its desktop tools, you can follow computer-use workflows in the same desktop and step in yourself: operate graphical apps, inspect generated documents or handle a step that needs manual input. Requires an Open Terminal connection with desktop support enabled. Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit
  • 🌐 Browser tab for browser use and web app testing. Open websites and local development servers beside your chat, with navigation controls, multiple tabs and a mobile viewport. On a compatible Open Terminal connection, Chrome mode gives you and the model a shared browser session for browser automation: navigate sites, interact with forms and test the web apps the model builds. You can watch the work and interact with the page yourself; Proxy mode remains available for previews. Requires browser support on the selected terminal, and Chrome availability for browser-use tools. Commit, Commit, Commit
  • ↔️ Full-width tabs. On larger screens, expand the tabbed workspace to fill the chat area, with the main conversation kept as its own tab. Switch between the chat, code, browser and desktop with more room to work, or return to the side-by-side layout; your layout choice is remembered. Commit, Commit
  • 💻 Open WebUI Desktop 0.1.x. The separately installed app for macOS, Windows and Linux now focuses on setting up and running Open WebUI on your own computer, with optional llama.cpp local models. The 0.1.0–0.1.4 updates bring a slimmer interface, searchable settings, startup logs, optional automatic Desktop updates, start-to-tray controls and image copying and saving. They also improve screen sharing, knowledge folder uploads, Linux graphics and shortcuts, and NVIDIA/AMD local-model setup and updates. Use it for a managed local installation and local AI workflows. Desktop changelog, Download v0.1.4
  • 🌿 Git in the side panel. When the selected terminal's folder is a Git repository, a Git panel in the tabbed side panel now lets you review diffs, stage, discard and commit changes, manage branches and worktrees, push and pull, browse history and work with GitHub pull requests, and open files can show their changes with Show diff. Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit, Commit
  • ⚡ Live terminal updates. On terminals that support it, the Git panel, the list of open ports and the running processes and their output now update as soon as something changes instead of every few seconds. Commit, Commit
  • 💭 Side chats. Typing "/side" or "/btw" in a chat, or choosing Side chat in the side panel, now opens a temporary side conversation using the chat so far as context. Ask a quick question or explore an alternative without adding the detour to the main conversation; the side chat disappears when you close its tab. Available to administrators and users given the new Allow Side Chat permission, which is off by default. Commit, Commit, Commit
  • 💬 Comment threads.
